title: Five Oceans
objective: After this level you can name and compare the five oceans.
summary: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic: biggest to smallest. The Southern Ocean is bounded by a current at 60° S; NOAA and National Geographic count it.

cards.headline: One ocean on the map has no coastline on its northern side.
cards.body: Its southern edge is Antarctica. Its northern edge is a line drawn across open water at 60° south. To see why, meet all five named oceans, biggest first.

items.label: The giant
points: Holds more than half of Earth's free water
All the continents could fit inside it

cards.headline: The ocean drawn by a current
cards.body: Historically there were four named oceans: the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian and Arctic, each defined by the continents around it. The Southern Ocean is different. It is defined by a current that flows all the way around Antarctica, and its northern edge is set at 60° south. Its border is a line through moving water. Good luck putting up a fence.

cards.headline: Five oceans, one asterisk
cards.body: The US Board on Geographic Names has used the name Southern Ocean since 1999, NOAA counts it as the fifth ocean, and National Geographic began recognizing it on June 8, 2021. The International Hydrographic Organization, which publishes the standard limits of oceans and seas, dropped it in 1953. In 2023 it voted to recognize it again, while leaving each member country free to keep its own view. So: five oceans, most of the time.
cards.callout: 1953: dropped · 1999: US name · 2021: National Geographic · 2023: IHO vote
